subject: Vocabulary
topic: Antonyms and Synonyms Mixed — SSC CGL Vocabulary (W11 B2)

questions.explanation: B is correct. COGENT = clear, logical, and convincing; a cogent argument is one that is powerfully persuasive. Synonyms: compelling, convincing, persuasive, valid. Antonym: weak, unconvincing. Trap: 'Vague' and 'irrelevant' are antonyms of cogent; 'Weak' is the antonym (a cogent argument is strong, not weak).

C is correct. BELLIGERENT = hostile and aggressive; eager to fight or argue. Antonym = peaceful, pacifist, amicable. Trap: Aggressive, Warlike, Hostile are all synonyms of belligerent; only Peaceful is the antonym.

B is correct. TACITURN = habitually silent; reluctant to talk. Synonyms: reserved, reticent, uncommunicative, withdrawn. Trap: Talkative, Expressive, Outgoing are all antonyms of taciturn — they describe someone who talks a lot. Reserved is the correct synonym (choosing not to express feelings openly).

C is correct. LOQUACIOUS = tending to talk a great deal; talkative. Antonym = TACITURN (habitually silent and reserved). Trap: Verbose (using too many words), Garrulous (excessively talkative), Voluble (speaking at length easily) are ALL synonyms of loquacious. Only Taciturn is the antonym. This is a hard question because all distractors are synonyms in a field where synonyms cluster.

C is correct. INTREPID = fearless and adventurous; remarkably brave in the face of danger. Synonyms: fearless, bold, dauntless, audacious, valiant. Trap: Timid and Cowardly are antonyms; Cautious = careful (not the same as fearless).

C is correct. PARSIMONIOUS = excessively unwilling to spend money; extremely stingy. Antonym = Generous (willing to give freely). Trap: Miserly, Frugal, Thrifty are all related to not spending money and are near-synonyms of parsimonious. Generous is the only antonym. Note: Frugal and Thrifty have a positive connotation (careful with money) while Parsimonious has a negative connotation (excessively stingy).

B is correct. ELUCIDATE = to make clear; to explain or clarify. Example: 'Could you elucidate your point?' Synonyms: clarify, explain, illuminate, expound. Trap: Confuse, Obscure, Complicate are all antonyms of elucidate (they add confusion rather than clarity). Root: Latin 'elucidare' = to make light/clear ('lux' = light).

C is correct. TRANSIENT = lasting only for a short time; temporary; fleeting. Antonym = Permanent (lasting forever or a very long time). Trap: Fleeting, Momentary, Ephemeral are all synonyms of transient (all mean brief/short-lived). Permanent is the correct antonym.

C is correct. LACONIC = using very few words; brief and concise in speech or expression. Origin: from the ancient Spartans (Laconians), who were famously terse. Synonyms: brief, concise, terse, pithy, succinct. Trap: Verbose (using too many words), Wordy (long-winded), Elaborate (detailed and complicated) are all antonyms of laconic.

C is correct. GREGARIOUS = fond of company; sociable; enjoying the company of others. Antonym = Reclusive (avoiding the company of others; hermit-like). Trap: Sociable, Outgoing, Friendly are synonyms of gregarious. Reclusive is the antonym (a recluse avoids social contact). Root: Latin 'gregarius' = belonging to a flock/herd ('grex' = flock).
